steps: Test option (A): Villi are finger-like mucosal projections in the small intestine for absorption, not lymphoid aggregates.
Test option (B): Peyer's patches are indeed aggregates of lymphoid tissue (GALT) found primarily in the ileum, the distal portion of the small intestine.
Test option (C): Rugae are folds found in the stomach lining, not lymphoid tissue in the small intestine.
Test option (D): Choroid plexus is a network of blood vessels in the brain ventricles that produces cerebrospinal fluid.
Elimination leaves only (B) as the correct anatomical structure.
